series.name: Life Time Grand Prix
series.tagline: Pro cycling's off-road championship series: seven races, one overall title.
series.description: The Life Time Grand Prix is professional off-road cycling's season-long championship. Launched in 2022, it scores an invited and qualified pro field across Life Time's biggest gravel and mountain bike races. For 2027 that means 25 women and 25 men racing seven events, from Sea Otter in April to the Sugar races in Bentonville, with each rider's best six results counting. The mix of 200-mile gravel and high-altitude mountain biking rewards complete off-road riders over specialists.
series.history: Life Time launched the Grand Prix in 2022 as the first true championship series for off-road cycling. The concept was simple but transformative: take the marquee events that Life Time already owned or partnered with — Unbound, Leadville, Sea Otter, Big Sugar, and Chequamegon — and create a points-based series that would crown an overall champion. The inaugural season immediately elevated the profile of every constituent race, drawing mainstream sports media attention and creating season-long storylines. Keegan Swenson won the first men's title; Lauren De Crescenzo took the women's. The lineup has changed most seasons. For 2027 it runs seven events, The Rad Dirt Fest returns, and a new Sea Otter qualifier fills 14 of the 25 places in each field.
series.format_overview: In 2027, 25 women and 25 men race seven events across gravel and mountain bike. The top 10 in each field from the 2026 standings and the top 2026 U23 rider get automatic invitations; the other 14 places go through the Sea Otter Grand Prix Qualifier, which combines Sea Otter Classic Gravel and the Fuego XL. Riders must start at least six events and their best six results count, so anyone who finishes all seven drops the lowest score. Points are awarded based on finish position at each event (1st place = 100 points, 2nd = 95, 3rd = 92, scaling down).
